abstract: The identification of isochromosome 12p [i(12p)] and 12p gains have significant clinical utility in the diagnosis of germ cell tumors (GCTs). We have summarized the results of fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) assays to identify i(12p), performed in a Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA)-validated setting for 536 specimens. In addition, the American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) Project GENIE registry and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) data sets were evaluated for chromosome 12p gains, and a limited number of cases were concurrently evaluated using FISH, single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) arrays and next-generation sequencing (NGS; including mate-pair sequencing). Specimens submitted for FISH testing were frequently from potential sites of metastases (male: 70.9% and female: 69.3%), and polysomy of chromosome 12 with or without concurrent i(12p) was a frequent finding, seen in 3% (16/536) and 35% (186/536) of cases, respectively. Our analysis suggests that 12p gains are likely to be present in approximately 73% of male GCT and in 32% of female GCT (AACR GENIE, n = 555). When comparing TCGA cases of testicular GCT (n = 149) to combined cases of sarcoma, colorectal, prostate, and urothelial carcinoma (n = 1754), 12p gains had a sensitivity of 77.2% and specificity of 97.3% for GCT. Some advantages of FISH over SNP arrays/NGS include relatively lower cost, rapid turnaround time, the ability to analyze biopsy material with a limited number of tumor cells (50 cells), and the ability to distinguish i(12p) from polysomy. The ability to spatially restrict the analysis to cells of interest is critical, as specimens submitted for testing often have low tumor purity. Disadvantages include false negative results due to an inability to detect segmental gains due to FISH probe design. With the availability of numerous testing modalities, including FISH, SNP arrays, and NGS-based assays, a nuanced understanding of the advantages and disadvantages of each methodology, as has been presented in this study, may inform appropriate testing strategies.
abstract_ja: イソクロモソーム12p [i(12p)] および12p獲得の同定は、胚細胞腫瘍(GCT)の診断において重要な臨床的有用性を持つ。我々は、CLIA(臨床検査室改善修正法)で妥当性が確認された環境において、536検体についてi(12p)を同定するための蛍光in situハイブリダイゼーション(FISH)アッセイの結果をまとめた。さらに、米国癌研究学会(AACR)のProject GENIEレジストリおよびThe Cancer Genome Atlas(TCGA)データセットを評価して染色体12p獲得を調べ、限られた数の症例について、FISH、一塩基多型(SNP)アレイ、次世代シーケンシング(NGS;メイトペアシーケンシングを含む)を同時に評価した。FISH検査に提出された検体は、転移の可能性がある部位に由来することが多く(男性70.9%、女性69.3%)、i(12p)の有無にかかわらず染色体12のポリソミーが頻繁に認められ、それぞれ症例の3%(16/536)および35%(186/536)で見られた。我々の解析によると、12p獲得は男性GCTの約73%、女性GCTの32%に存在すると考えられる(AACR GENIE、n = 555)。精巣GCTのTCGA症例(n = 149)を、肉腫、大腸癌、前立腺癌、尿路上皮癌の併合症例(n = 1754)と比較すると、12p獲得はGCTに対して感度77.2%、特異度97.3%であった。FISHがSNPアレイ/NGSに優る利点として、比較的低コスト、迅速な結果報告、腫瘍細胞数が限られた生検材料(50細胞)の解析が可能であること、およびi(12p)とポリソミーを区別できることが挙げられる。腫瘍含有率の低い検体が多いため、関心のある細胞に解析を空間的に限定できることは極めて重要である。欠点として、FISHプローブの設計上、部分的な獲得を検出できないことによる偽陰性の結果がある。FISH、SNPアレイ、NGSベースのアッセイを含む多数の検査法が利用可能となった現在、本研究で示されたように各手法の利点と欠点を的確に理解することは、適切な検査戦略の策定に資すると考えられる。
